info.title: Entitler customers service
info.description: Customers, their tracks, subscriptions, add-ons, grants, meters and usage, and the entitlements derived from them as of now or the Entitler-As-Of instant, from the release or change each customer's track serves. Also each environment's tracks, their rollouts, its connections to payment providers, the listings of each release and change on them, and the pricing on sale through each track. Nothing is derived on a schedule.

servers.description: For the dashboard: the session cookie and credentialed CORS.

key.description: A project key: a secret key starts `ent_test_` for a test environment or `ent_live_` for a live one, a publishable key `ent_pk_test_` or `ent_pk_live_`, then 32 letters and digits; keys minted before environments had kinds keep `ent_` alone. It names its project and environment and carries the scopes chosen when it was minted. Only a publishable key may send `Entitler-Identity-Token`.

orgKey.description: An organisation key, `ent_org_` and 32 letters and digits, with the scopes chosen when it was minted. It names the project and environment with the Entitler-Project and Entitler-Environment headers.

session.description: The access token `POST /auth/sign-in` returns on api.entitler.dev: a person, with the scopes of their role in the organisation of the project the request names.

sessionCookie.name: __Secure-entitler_session
sessionCookie.description: The same access token as an HttpOnly cookie, which api.entitler.app sets for the dashboard.

customerToken.description: A customer token from `POST /customers/{externalId}/tokens`: one customer, for at most an hour, with a subset of `entitlements:read`, `usage:read` and `usage:write`.

identityToken.name: Entitler-Identity-Token
identityToken.description: An identity token from a sign-in provider registered on the key's project, sent beside the key. It names the customer, `me`.

by.description: The name of the key or person that made the change, or `null` for one that came with time.

reason.description: Why, as the write gave it, or `null`.

quantity.description: How many they hold after it: 0 removes it, and above 1 needs a countable add-on.

sku.description: The Apple or Google SKU the customer bought the add-on with, which records the store as its biller and never touches Stripe; refused with `409 billed_elsewhere` when Stripe bills the product.

title.description: The rule in a few words, such as `Two plans in one product`.

customer.description: The customer the alert is about, or `null` for an event no customer here owns.

seenAt.description: When the provider last reported the state that raised it.

resolvedBy.description: `provider` when the provider matched the rules again, `person` when someone resolved it.

customer.description: The customer's name, or `null` when no customer here owns the event.

connection.description: The connection's name, such as `Stripe rest of world`.

product.description: The product the rule is about.

plans.description: The plans the provider bills, by name.

held.description: The plan the customer holds in Entitler.

ids.description: The provider's id, such as a Stripe price id.

boughtThrough.description: The connection the customer bought their plan through.

next.description: Pass as `before` for the next page, or `null` at the end.

key.description: A Stripe restricted key with write access to Customers, Checkout Sessions, Subscriptions, Customer portal and Webhook Endpoints, and read access to Prices, Invoices, PaymentIntents, Charges and Accounts. Entitler stores it encrypted and never shows it again, and reads the account's mode from it. A test environment refuses a live-mode key.

key.description: A new restricted key for a Stripe connection, with write access to Customers, Checkout Sessions, Subscriptions, Customer portal and Webhook Endpoints, and read access to Prices, Invoices, PaymentIntents, Charges and Accounts, such as after rolling a leaked key. It must be for the same Stripe account and mode. Entitler creates a new webhook endpoint with it, keeps the key and the endpoint's secret encrypted, and deletes the old endpoint. The connection keeps its id, so its customers, purchases and listings stay with it.

previousTrackId.description: The track a verified production build returns them to.

payment.description: With `402 payment_required`: the payment a plan change waits on. The customer keeps their plan until it succeeds.

listingGaps.description: With `409 listing_gaps`: the gaps a rollout or experiment start would leave.

listingProblems.description: With `409 listing_invalid`: the listings whose Stripe price fails the checks.

ExperimentAssignment.description: The experiment the caller is in, and their arm.

total.description: How much they used in all, the sum of the amounts.

lastAt.description: When they last used it, up to the instant.

renewsAt.description: When the plan renews, or `null` when it does not.

billedBy.description: The store or provider that bills the plan, or `null` when nothing bills it.

token.description: The snapshot: a compact JWS signed with ES256, `typ` `entitlements+jwt`, to keep and verify offline.

expiresAt.description: When the snapshot stops verifying, its `exp`.

keyId.description: The `kid` of the key that signed it, one of `GET /customers/snapshot-keys`.

period.description: The billing period's label, empty for a one-time plan.

anyOf.description: The provider's ids for the plan and billing period, shaped like the connector's SKU ids: `priceId` for Stripe, `productId` for the App Store, `productId` and `basePlanId` for Google Play.

ids.description: `null` marks the plan and period as not sold through the channel.

period.description: The billing period's label, empty for a one-time plan.

anyOf.description: The provider's ids for the plan and billing period, shaped like the connector's SKU ids: `priceId` for Stripe, `productId` for the App Store, `productId` and `basePlanId` for Google Play.

ids.description: `null` marks the plan and period as not sold through the channel.

state.description: `listed` with ids, `not_sold` when marked not sold here, `blank` when left empty.

source.description: `set` when entered for this catalogue, `carried` when taken from the previous release because the plan version is unchanged, `null` for a blank.

price.description: The price Stripe holds for a Stripe price id, read through the connection, or `null` when it cannot be read. Left out for store channels, whose prices come from the device.

kind.description: `stops_selling`: the track sells it on the channel today and the new catalogue leaves it blank there. `unlisted`: a self-serve plan and period with no ids on any of the environment's connections. An environment with no connection has no gaps.

ListingGap.description: A plan and billing period a listing leaves blank. Sales-led plans never have gaps.

ListingKey.description: The catalogue a listing sells: a release by its number, or a change by its id. A change's listings sell it on a testers track that follows it and in an experiment's variant, and carry to the release it becomes.

ListingKeyInput.description: The catalogue a listing sells: a release by its number, or a change by its id. A change's listings sell it on a testers track that follows it and in an experiment's variant, and carry to the release it becomes.

problem.description: `price_not_found` when the Stripe connection has no such price, `price_inactive` when it is archived, `interval_mismatch` when it bills on another interval than the billing period, or recurs for a one-time plan.

ListingsInput.description: Listings for the new catalogue on the environment's connections. A plan version unchanged since the track's current release keeps its listing on the same channel unless one is sent.

reason.description: Why, in at most 200 characters, shown in the customer's activity.

actor.description: The person or system that decided, such as a support agent or `hubspot`, shown in the customer's activity beside the key's name.

by.description: How far to move the meter, up or down; it never goes below 0.

to.description: The value to set the meter to.

anchor.description: Where windows start: `period`, the default, from the start of the customer's billing period, the period's end closing the last window early; `calendar`, on calendar boundaries in the project's time zone (hours from local midnight, days from 1 January 1970, weeks from Monday, months from January).

Money.description: `real` for money that is charged, `test` for test money that is never charged.

Move.description: `subscribe` from no plan in a product, `upgrade`, `downgrade` or `switch` (neither up nor down) to another plan, `add` an add-on, or `replace` an add-on by another.

default.description: True for a product's default plan.

product.description: The product the move is in, or `null` for an add-on for every product.

from.description: The plan or add-on the move starts from, or `null` for sign-up.

action.description: `buy`: the customer can make the move alone. `contact`: a sales-led move, which only the company can make. `unavailable`: neither can make it now; `reason` says why.

reason.description: A sentence for the developer saying why the move is `unavailable`, else `null`.

periods.description: The plan's billing periods, from the catalogue, whatever sells them.

skus.description: The SKUs an app passes to Stripe, StoreKit or Play Billing to buy the plan in this environment, for each billing period.

period.description: The billing period it sells, or `null` for none.

connector.description: Where it is bought: `stripe`, `apple` or `google`, or another connector.

price.description: The price the provider charges, read through the environment's connection to the provider, or `null` when it cannot be read. Left out where the environment has no connection.

PackageName.description: The Google Play app's package name, such as `com.example.app`.

status.description: Why the payment has not succeeded: the card was declined, the customer must confirm it (such as 3D Secure), the provider is still processing it, or the provider gave no reason.

url.description: The provider's page where the customer pays or confirms it, or null.

PeriodKey.description: The billing period's key: its label in lower case, with a hyphen for each run of other characters, such as `monthly` or `every-2-weeks`. It stays the same however the label is shown.

period.description: The billing period, or `null` for a one-time plan.

name.description: The connection's name, such as Stripe rest of world.

mode.description: A Stripe connection's mode: `test` when its purchases use test money, so an app can show "Test purchase, no charge". `null` for a store, where the device decides.

purchasable.description: True when a listing sells the plan for the period through the channel. A plan without one still shows, and checkout through the channel is refused with `409 not_listed`. A test-mode Stripe connection's listings are never purchasable on a live environment's track that is not for testers, so test money never pays for a real customer.

ids.description: The ids to pass to Stripe, StoreKit or Play Billing to buy the plan, or `null` when it is not purchasable through the channel.

price.description: The price Stripe holds, read through the connection, or `null` when it cannot be read. Left out for store channels, whose prices come from the device.

channels.description: Each of the environment's connections, oldest first, with its ids for the plan and period and whether the caller can buy it there. With two connections of one provider, such as Stripe for two regions, the app chooses which ids to use.

key.description: The key to send back in writes, such as `monthly`.

label.description: The label to show, such as Monthly.

product.description: The product changed, or `null` for an add-on for every product.

plan.description: The plan or add-on the change leaves the customer on, or `null` when they are left with no plan in that product.

quantity.description: An add-on's quantity after the change, 0 when removed; `null` for a plan.

effective.description: `now`, or `renewal` when the change waits for the end of the period.

until.description: When the customer returns to the default plan, or `null`.

changed.description: False when nothing changed: a cancel with nothing to cancel, an undo with nothing booked, a plan they already hold.

from.description: The plan they held before the override.

period.description: The billing period of the plan they held before, or `null` for none.

billedBy.description: The connection that kept billing them for the plan they held before, or `null` when nothing billed them.

PlanOverride.description: A move made in Entitler only with `billing: keep`, as a deliberate exception: the payment provider keeps billing the plan they held before.

plan.description: The plan, by its key or public id, or `null` to end their plan in `product`, which moves them to its default plan when it has one.

product.description: The product whose plan `plan: null` ends, by key. Only with `plan: null`.

sku.description: The SKU the customer bought, in place of `plan`: the plan, and the billing period, it sells in this environment. A SKU an older version sold still names its plan.

when.description: `now`, or `end` for the renewal; the project's policy when left out.

billing.description: `provider` charges the change through the provider that bills the product. `keep` moves the customer in Entitler while the provider keeps billing the plan it bills, until a later change. `end` ends the provider’s subscription when the change takes effect, and the customer then holds the plan outside any provider.

until.description: An RFC 3339 instant in the future: at `until` the customer returns to the product’s default plan, unless a later change moved them or set a later `until`. Refused while Stripe bills the product, unless `billing` is `end`.

version.description: `latest` moves a customer who already holds the plan to its latest version, as a rollout would.

register.description: True to register a customer who is not registered yet first, for a credential with `customers:register` or `customers:write`; without it a missing customer is `404 customer_not_found`.

reason.description: Why, in at most 200 characters, shown in the customer's activity.

actor.description: The person or system that decided, such as a support agent or `hubspot`, shown in the customer's activity beside the key's name.

track.description: The track the caller resolved to.

release.description: The number of the release the answer comes from, or `null` when the track follows a change or runs nothing yet.

change.description: The id of the change the answer comes from: the change a testers track follows, or an experiment's change for its variant.

testers.description: True on a track for testers, and in a test environment, where test money is taken. Each channel says whether its own purchases use test money.

experiment.description: The experiment and arm the caller is in, or `null`.

customer.description: The customer's external id, or `null` for a signed-out caller.

plans.description: The plans on sale to the caller.

product.description: The product's key, or `null` for an add-on for every product.

salesLed.description: True for a tier to ask about: only sales-led paths reach it from sign-up.

listings.description: Each billing period and where it is sold.

from.description: The release the track ran before, if any.

rollback.description: True when it points the track at an older release.

state.description: `pending` while it waits for a second person to approve it, `running` once the track runs the release while its moves are still being recorded (Entitler resumes them within two hours if the rollout stopped part way), `done` once every move is recorded, `failed` when it could not finish or a later rollout replaced it while it ran, `declined` when it was declined or withdrawn before it ran.

requesterId.description: The id of the person who requested it, or null when a key requested it.

acceptedGaps.description: The gaps the person rolling out accepted, or empty.

moved.description: How many of the track's customers its moves moved to a newer version.

cohortMoves.description: The move chosen for each cohort in place of its version’s, or empty.

cohortChoices.description: The cohorts `cohortMoves` names, in the preview's order, each with its plan, its name and the move chosen for it, so whoever approves the rollout can read them.

id.description: The cohort as `<plan id>:<n>`, the key `cohortMoves` takes.

customers.description: How many of the track's customers in the cohort hold an older version the rollout can move them from.

move.description: The move the plan's new version sets, which the rollout makes for the cohort unless `cohortMoves` names another.

name.description: The cohort's name when the rollout was asked for.

channels.description: The new release's listings on each of the environment's connections: those sent, then those carried over, then blanks.

gaps.description: Rolling out with gaps needs `acceptGaps`; otherwise it is refused with `409 listing_gaps`.

problems.description: Stripe price ids that fail the checks. Rolling out is refused with `409 listing_invalid` while any remain.

moves.description: How many of the track's customers each plan's moves would move, and when, with the `cohortMoves` sent.

cohorts.description: For each plan whose version changes for the track's customers, its cohorts holding them, newest first, with their default moves.

approvalRequired.description: True when the environment's protection needs a second person to approve it, which it does only while the project's releases and reviews switches are on and the organisation's plan has `review_flow`.

caughtUp.description: True when the track would then match All customers.

release.description: The release the rollout would point the track at.

cohortMoves.description: A move for each cohort, named `<plan key or id>:<n>` as the preview's `cohorts` name them, in place of the move the plan's new version sets: `stay` keeps the cohort's customers on their version, `renewal` moves them at their renewal and `now` moves them at once. A cohort left out takes the version's move. Moved customers stay in their cohort.

caughtUp.description: True when the track now matches All customers, so it can be kept, caught up, or closed.

ids.description: The provider's ids for the price billed, such as `priceId` for Stripe.

sale.description: The listing that sells these ids, or `null` when none does.

amount.description: The amount in the currency's smallest unit, such as cents, as the provider charges it.

currency.description: The ISO 4217 code, in lower case, as the provider gives it.

interval.description: How often it is charged, or `null` for a one-time price.

version.description: The release the listing is in, or `null` for the open change.

period.description: The billing period the listing sells, empty for a one-time sale.

product.description: The plan's product id, or `null` for a customer-wide add-on.

status.description: The provider's own status, such as `active`, `trialing` or `canceled`.

billing.description: Whether the provider bills it now.

key.description: The key to send back in writes, such as `monthly`.

channel.description: The connection it was bought through, or `null` for a change made by hand.

release.description: The number of the release it was bought from, or `null` when bought from a change.

change.description: The id of the change it was bought from: one a testers track follows, or an experiment's change.

arm.description: The experiment arm it was bought in, if any.

Purchase.description: Where a plan or add-on was bought, and with real or test money.

connectionId.description: The connection the event came through, or `null` when it is not known.

eventId.description: The provider's id for the event.

reason.description: `real_money_in_test_environment` when real money reached a test environment, `test_money_on_real_money_track` when test money paid for a plan on a track not for testers, `sandbox_builds_turned_off` when a store sandbox purchase came from a customer not on a testers track.

items.description: The newest refused payment events first, at most 100.

story.description: Whether the sample also wrote its rollout story: the Beta track and its cohort.

connector.description: Where it was bought: `stripe`, `apple` or `google`, or another connector.

started.description: The new cohort, open: new subscribers to the plan join it.

closed.description: The cohort it closed, which keeps its customers, or none when the plan had none open.

plan.description: The plan or add-on, by its key or public id.

quantity.description: For a countable add-on: how many they hold after it, 1 when added.

returnUrl.description: Where the provider's page sends the customer back to, paid or not: Stripe Checkout's success and cancel page, and the return from a confirmation. A change that needs a page and has none is refused with `400 return_url_required` before anything changes.

register.description: True to register a customer who is not registered yet first, for a credential with `customers:register` or `customers:write`; without it a missing customer is `404 customer_not_found`.

product.description: The product changed, or `null` for an add-on for every product.

plan.description: The plan or add-on the change leaves the customer on, or `null` when they are left with no plan in that product.

quantity.description: An add-on's quantity after the change, 0 when removed; `null` for a plan.

effective.description: `now`, or `renewal` when the change waits for the end of the period.

until.description: When the customer returns to the default plan, or `null`.

changed.description: False when nothing changed: a cancel with nothing to cancel, an undo with nothing booked, a plan they already hold.

next.description: Nothing changes until the customer pays on the page.

url.description: The provider's page: Stripe Checkout, or a confirmation.

next.description: The provider is still confirming a payment; the change follows when it succeeds.

everyone.description: True for the environment's All customers track, which is last and never closes.

release.description: The number of the release the track runs, or `null` when it follows a change.

change.description: The id of the open change a testers track follows, or `null` when it runs a release.

testers.description: True for a track for testers: it may follow an open change, takes test money, and its customers count as test customers. A test environment's tracks are always for testers.

experimentId.description: The experiment running on the track, if any.

caughtUp.description: True when it runs the same release as All customers, for the same customers, with no experiment running.

track.description: The name of the track to put the customer on, which is unique in the environment and the same in every environment, or `null` for All customers.

testers.description: Makes it a track for testers. Left out, it is for testers only in a test environment, whose tracks always are.

change.description: An open change for a testers track to follow, in place of a release.

sources.description: Where the value comes from, each with its share of the value: the plan, then any grants, add-ons and banked credits that add to it. Empty when nothing gives the feature.

held.description: How much open holds reserve this period or window; counted in `remaining`.

experiment.description: The experiment and arm the caller is in, or `null`.

firstAt.description: When the environment first answered an entitlement check from a project or organisation key, a customer token or an identity token, or `null` until it has. Checks from a dashboard session do not count.

test.description: How many of the customers are test customers, whose every purchase used test money, or members of test-money tracks, whether or not `includeTest` counts them. When it is `0`, `includeTest` changes nothing.

addOns.description: The add-ons for every product the customer holds.

plans.description: The base plan held in each product, first product first.

defaultPlan.description: The default plan a customer not registered yet reads as in their first product, or `null`. A registered customer holds their plan, so it is always `null` for them.

testCustomer.description: True when every purchase the customer made used test money.

quantity.description: How many they hold. Each one adds the add-on's numbers.

countable.description: Whether they can hold more than one, which needs a number in the add-on to add.

change.description: The id of the change the answer comes from: the change a testers track follows, or an experiment's change for its variant.

TrackedSnapshotClaims.description: The payload of a signed entitlements snapshot from `POST /customers/{externalId}/snapshots`, an ES256 JWS with `typ` `entitlements+jwt`, verified against `GET /customers/snapshot-keys`.

period.description: How often the plan is billed, or `null` for none.

renewsAt.description: When the period ends: the plan renews, booked changes take effect and metered allowances start again. For a plan billed through Stripe this is the end of the period Stripe bills, or the earlier instant Stripe cancels it.

anyOf.description: The period Stripe last reported for a plan billed through it, which Entitler follows: its start and end, when a trial ends, and when Stripe cancels the subscription. `null` when Entitler sets the period itself.

until.description: When the customer returns to the default plan, as `PUT /customers/{externalId}/plan` set it, or `null`.

billing.description: Who bills the plan from renewal: `provider` the payment provider, `outside` no payment provider.

movingTo.description: The default plan the customer moves to when the plan ends, as it was when they cancelled, or `null` when they are left with no plan.

override.description: The override that put them on this plan, until a later `PUT /customers/{externalId}/plan` ends it.

customer.description: The external id of the one customer the report covers, or null for every customer.

sources.description: Where the value comes from, each with its share of the value: the plan, then any grants, add-ons and banked credits that add to it. Empty when nothing gives the feature.

held.description: How much open holds reserve this period or window; counted in `remaining`.

outcome.description: What happened: `recorded`, `duplicate` (a replay of an earlier request, which stands), `refused`, `held`, `settled`, `released`, `cancelled` (the report, or the report a replayed key names, is cancelled) or `adjusted` (a meter set).

refusal.description: Why a gated report or a hold was refused; null otherwise.

id.description: The report this created, repeated, settled or cancelled.

holdId.description: The hold this created, settled, released or repeated.

amount.description: The amount asked for, or the original’s on a replay.

meterChange.description: How much this request moved the meter: the amount recorded or settled, minus what came off when cancelled, the difference when set, else 0.

overBy.description: How far `used` is past the allowance after the write; 0 within it or unlimited.

late.description: The report’s period or window had closed when it arrived: it is in the log and the usage report, not on the meter.

expiresAt.description: When the hold expires; null for a report.

track.description: The track the caller resolved to.

release.description: The number of the release the answer comes from, or `null` when the track follows a change or runs nothing yet.

change.description: The id of the change the answer comes from: the change a testers track follows, or an experiment's change for its variant.

testers.description: True on a track for testers, and in a test environment, where test money is taken. Each channel says whether its own purchases use test money.

experiment.description: The experiment and arm the caller is in, or `null`.

sellable.description: Every plan and billing period the catalogue sells, whether or not the environment has a connection to list them on.

gaps.description: The gaps in the track's current listings, so the dashboard can flag them on the track, and on the change a testers track follows, which has no rollout step.

name.description: The connection's name, such as Stripe rest of world.

cells.description: Every plan and billing period the catalogue sells, listed or not.

sharedWith.description: The other open tracks of the environment selling the same catalogue, which these listings also apply to.

channels.description: Each channel's listings for the catalogue, replacing that channel's listings. Channels left out keep theirs.

release.description: The release to point the track at. An older one rolls back.

cohortMoves.description: A move for each cohort, named `<plan key or id>:<n>` as the preview's `cohorts` name them, in place of the move the plan's new version sets: `stay` keeps the cohort's customers on their version, `renewal` moves them at their renewal and `now` moves them at once. A cohort left out takes the version's move. Moved customers stay in their cohort.

acceptGaps.description: Rolls out despite the gaps the preview reports. Without it, a rollout with gaps is refused with `409 listing_gaps`, listing them.

TrackSource.description: The source of the customer's place on their track: the customer's server, a person in the dashboard, or a verified sandbox build of their app.

testers.description: Makes it a track for testers, or not. Members' subscriptions bought with test money end when it stops being for testers in a live environment. All customers and a test environment's tracks keep theirs.

change.description: An open change for a testers track to follow in place of its current release. Once the change is released, the track runs that release.

action.description: `buy`: the customer can make the move alone. `contact`: a sales-led move, which only the company can make. `unavailable`: neither can make it now; `reason` says why.

reason.description: A sentence for the developer saying why the move is `unavailable`, else `null`.

by.description: The name of the key or person that recorded it, or `null`.

actor.description: The person or system that decided an adjustment, or the cancel of a report, as the write named it, or `null`.

reason.description: Why the adjustment, or the cancel of a report, was made, or `null`.

cancelledAt.description: When the report was cancelled, as of the instant read; null while it stands.

setTo.description: The value the meter was set to.

occurredAt.description: When the usage happened, an RFC 3339 instant with an offset: at most the project's `offlineDays` before the write and 5 minutes after it. The write's instant when left out.

idempotencyKey.description: The event's key, 1 to 200 printable ASCII characters, scoped to the customer.

index.description: The event’s position in the request, from 0.

id.description: The report recorded, or the one a duplicate repeats.

error.description: Why the event was not recorded, with the code a single report would answer.

register.description: Register customers who are not registered yet. Needs `customers:register` or `customers:write`.

state.description: `open` until settled, released or past `expiresAt`, when it is `expired`.

ttlSeconds.description: How long the hold lasts before it expires on its own, at most an hour.

post.description: What `GET /customers/{externalId}/entitlements` answers for the customer, signed so an app can keep it and check entitlements without a connection until it expires. The token is a compact JWS signed with ES256, with `typ` `entitlements+jwt` and the signing key's `kid` in its header, and `iss`, `sub` (the customer's external id), `environment` (its `id`), `track` (its `id` and `name`), `release` or `change` (the catalogue the customer's track serves), `testers` (true on a track for testers and in a test environment), `entitlements`, `iat` and `exp` in its payload; verify it against `GET /customers/snapshot-keys`, from keys the app ships or fetches itself rather than keys stored beside the token. Every environment signs with the same key, so also check that `iss` is `https://api.entitler.dev/customers`, `sub` and `environment` name the customer and environment the app expects, and `iat` is not after now. It lasts the project's offline days unless `ttlSeconds` asks for less, and asking for more is refused. It expires no later than the first time-limited grant it holds ends, the customer's booked change or cancellation takes effect, or a meter it holds resets, so a snapshot never outlives the entitlements it signs. A customer not registered yet, or registered only after the instant, is answered with the default plan's entitlements, and nothing is written. Only a test environment signs a snapshot as of Entitler-As-Of, and its `iat` is then that instant. With a customer token or an identity token, `me` names the customer.

post.description: Records an amount of a metered feature used by the customer, with the credential's source, and answers with the customer's check for the feature after it and what happened in `outcome`. In `gate` mode, the default, the report is checked against the meter of its period or window, plus open holds, in the same write that records it: a report that does not fit, or of a feature the customer is not entitled to, is not stored and answers 200 with `outcome: "refused"` and `refusal` `over_allowance` or `not_entitled`, and the same key may succeed later. In `observe` mode the report is always recorded and `overBy` says how far the meter is past the allowance; `remaining` never goes below 0. `occurredAt` places the report in the period or window it happened in, at most the project's offline days before the write and 5 minutes after it; a report whose period had closed when it arrived is recorded with `late: true`, in the log and the usage report but not on the meter. Every report needs an `Idempotency-Key` header, scoped to the customer and never freed: a replay answers 200 with `duplicate`, or `cancelled` once the report was cancelled, and records nothing. `register: true` registers the customer first, for a credential with `customers:register` or `customers:write`, refusing an ID a customer cannot have with `400 invalid_body`; an `occurredAt` before a registration made by the same request counts from the registration's instant, so such a report must succeed on its first attempt: a retry dated before the registration is `400 invalid_occurred_at`. Each recorded report counts one `usage_reports` unit on the organisation's monthly quota; past it reports are still recorded and the organisation is alerted. A missing Idempotency-Key is `400 idempotency_key_required` and a malformed one `400 invalid_idempotency_key`; a body with an unknown field or a bad amount is `400 invalid_body`; a feature that is not metered is `400 not_metered`; an unregistered customer is `404 customer_not_found` and an unknown feature `404 feature_not_found`; a key used for another request is `422 idempotency_mismatch`. Reports from customer and identity tokens are limited to 100 every 10 seconds per customer, `429 rate_limited` beyond it. The body is at most 16 KB.

post.description: Reserves an amount of a metered feature against the customer's `remaining` for up to an hour, for work whose real cost is known only afterwards, and answers with the check after it, `outcome: "held"`, the `holdId` and `expiresAt`. A hold is always gated: one that does not fit the allowance, counting the meter and the open holds, or of a feature the customer is not entitled to, is not stored and answers 200 with `outcome: "refused"`. Settle it with the real amount, or release it; a hold neither settled nor released expires on its own at `expiresAt` and stops counting, so a crash never leaves the customer charged. post.summary: Subscribe or move a customer, as their own choice
post.description: The customer's own choice of a plan or an add-on, named by its key or public id, under self-serve rules: it must be one of the moves `GET /customers/{externalId}/plans` offers, along a self-serve path, or it is refused with `403 not_self_serve`. A plan subscribes them where they hold nothing in its product, moves them to it, or changes how often the plan they hold is billed when `period` names another period key; the project's policies decide whether a move takes effect now or at renewal. An add-on is added, has its quantity set when they already hold it, or replaces the add-on a `replace` move starts from. post.description: Replaces the customers flagged as samples with a fresh set on the catalogue the environment's All customers track serves, with their subscriptions, grants and usage, and never touches a customer created any other way. Right after `POST /plans/sample`, in an environment with no customers of your own, no tracks besides All customers and no rollouts, and without `Entitler-As-Of`, it also writes the sample's story in the same commit: All customers runs R1, Pro starts a Launch offer cohort, the customers join All customers's plans, a Beta track with test payments follows the open change with two sample customers on Team, and R2 is rolled out to All customers, keeping Pro's Version 1 signups where they are and moving the Launch offer at renewal. A track, a rollout or a customer of your own that appears meanwhile, a change to All customers or a cohort started at the same moment refuses it with 409 `stale`, and neither the customers nor the story are written. Called again, it puts two new sample customers back on that Beta track. Like the sample catalogue, the story leaves nothing out because of the organisation's Entitler plan: the Beta track and the cohort choices are written whatever its `tracks` limit and cohorts feature. Samples never count against the project's `live_customers` or `test_customers` limit. A test environment takes them, and so does the project's live environment while the environments switch is off, when live is its only environment; otherwise a live one is refused with 409, before the credential's scopes are checked. A customer of your own with an external id a sample uses refuses it with 409 naming that id. An environment takes new samples at most once a minute: a sooner call, or the later of two that race, is refused with 429 `rate_limited` and `Retry-After`, and the samples it replaces are deleted, not kept. The story needs the project's tracks switch, and is refused with 409 `switch_off` while it is off; the cohort it starts is written while the cohorts switch is off too, and shows once cohorts is turned on.

post.description: Records up to 500 usage events, of any customers of the environment, in observe mode: each is recorded whatever the allowance, in the period or window its `occurredAt` falls in, `late` when that had closed. Each event carries its own `idempotencyKey`, scoped to its customer and never freed. The answer is 200 with a result per event, in the order sent: `recorded`, `duplicate` (the key was used before for the same event, whose `id` and `late` it gives) or `error` with the code a single report would answer: `customer_not_found`, `feature_not_found`, `not_metered`, `invalid_occurred_at` and `idempotency_mismatch`, and with `register: true` also `invalid_body` for an ID a customer cannot have, `rate_limited` past the registration limits and `limit_reached` past the plan's customers. An error in one event never stops the others. `register: true` registers customers who are not registered yet, for a credential with `customers:register` or `customers:write`; each new customer spends the registration limits, and an event of a customer registered by the same request may be dated before the registration, when it counts from the registration's instant. A body that is not valid as a whole is `400 invalid_body` and records nothing. Keys only: customer and identity tokens are refused with `403 scope_required`. The request's own Idempotency-Key, which the SDKs send, is checked and ignored, since each event carries its key. A batch whose every event is a `duplicate` answers with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. Every recorded event counts one `usage_reports` unit. The body is at most 512 KB.

post.description: Where Stripe sends the events of a Stripe connection. post.summary: Roll out a release to a track
post.description: Points the track at a release, with the listings for it on the track's channels. An older release rolls back: new purchases and registrations see the older catalogue at once and customers already moved stay where they are. Gaps are refused with `409 listing_gaps` unless `acceptGaps` is true, and a Stripe price that fails the checks with `409 listing_invalid`; nothing is ever written to Stripe. While the organisation's plan lacks cohorts, a release whose new plan versions move customers, or `cohortMoves` that differ from the release's moves, is refused with `409 capability_required`. The track then runs the release, and the release's moves run for the track's customers who hold older versions in each plan's lineage, recorded as subscription events with the rollout's id, 500 customers at a time: the rollout is `running` until the last page lands and `done` after, and one that stops part way is resumed within two hours, skipping customers it already moved. Rolling back cancels the renewal moves newer releases booked for the track's customers, and a renewal move never takes a customer below the version they hold. When the environment's protection needs a second person, while the project's releases and reviews switches are on and the organisation's plan has `review_flow`, the rollout waits as `pending` (202) until someone else approves it with `POST /promotions/{id}/approve`; an owner nobody else may approve rollouts for in the environment rolls out at once. While a rollout of the track waits for approval, another is refused with `409`. `caughtUp` says whether the track now matches All customers, so it can be kept, caught up, or closed.
